name: Awesome Computer Use Ecosystem
licenseScope: Catalog content only; listed projects retain their own licenses.

projects.name: UI-TARS Desktop
projects.description: Desktop application with visual task execution, status feedback, and local or remote operators; shares its repository with Agent TARS and SDKs.

projects.name: UI-TARS SDK
projects.description: Embeddable screenshot-model-action loop with operator interfaces, events, and pause/stop controls; desktop integration uses a separate native input operator.

projects.name: UFO Desktop AgentOS
projects.description: Windows desktop agent coordinating applications through UIA, Win32, and COM, with screenshot observations, hybrid GUI/API actions, and reusable application knowledge.

projects.name: UFO Galaxy
projects.description: Cross-device task planning and orchestration using dynamic dependency graphs; delegates Windows desktop execution to UFO Desktop AgentOS.

projects.name: Agent S
projects.description: Desktop agent framework with a CLI and Python SDK, screenshot-based planning, grounding, and PyAutoGUI actions; requires model configuration and is distinct from hosted Sai.

projects.name: Midscene
projects.description: Visual automation framework with native desktop and remote Windows RDP support, a JavaScript SDK, Playground, AI assertions, and execution reports.

projects.name: Open Computer Use
projects.description: Open implementation of the Codex Computer Use execution layer, exposed through MCP with native accessibility, screenshot, and input backends.

projects.name: Open Browser Use
projects.description: Open implementation of the browser execution path reconstructed from the Codex Computer Use ecosystem, with a Chrome extension, CLI, MCP server, and JavaScript, Python, and Go SDKs.

projects.name: Codex Computer Use Reverse Engineering Lab
projects.description: Experiment-backed analysis of the macOS Codex Computer Use architecture, protocol, accessibility state, input path, policy gates, and lifecycle.

projects.name: Open Codex Computer History
projects.description: Clean-room event history for desktop interaction, with privacy filtering, summaries, search, MCP tools, and native macOS recording.

projects.name: Open Codex Record & Replay
projects.description: Open record-and-replay pipeline spanning native capture, session storage, evaluation, workflow controls, and reusable agent Skill generation.

projects.name: Anthropic Linux Computer Use Demo
projects.description: Reference agent loop with a containerized Linux desktop, screenshots, xdotool input, VNC, and Streamlit; Claude service access is separate.

projects.name: Anthropic macOS Computer Use Example
projects.description: macOS reference implementation with PyAutoGUI input, coordinate handling, batched tools, trajectory inspection, and debugging; not the source of a proprietary desktop product.

projects.name: Qwen Open Computer Use
projects.description: Qwen Code's cross-platform adaptation of Open Computer Use, distributed as an MCP service and command-line tool for Qwen Code and other agents.

projects.name: Qwen CUA Driver
projects.description: Qwen Code's vendored distribution of CUA Driver, with Qwen-owned product identity, patches, releases, and Python and TypeScript SDK integration.

projects.name: Kimi Computer Use
projects.description: Unofficial bridge that lets Kimi Code use an existing OpenAI Computer Use installation on macOS; it is separate from the proprietary KimiCU runtime.

projects.name: Kimi Computer Use Reverse Engineering Lab
projects.description: Static and controlled dynamic study of KimiCU 0.5.4, covering packaging, MCP, native modules, XPC trust, WebView input, and stale-element behavior.

projects.name: Open ZCode Computer Use
projects.description: Clean-room macOS implementation of the ZCode CUA 0.5.12 MCP contract, with all 30 tool schemas and independently implemented execution.

projects.name: CUA Driver
projects.description: Cross-platform desktop and browser automation runtime from CUA, available through MCP, CLI, native SDK bindings, and embeddable interfaces.

projects.name: CUA
projects.description: Sandboxes, SDKs, and benchmarks for building, training, and evaluating agents that operate full desktops.

projects.name: CUA Bench
projects.description: Desktop evaluation and reinforcement-learning environments with image provisioning, benchmark adapters, custom tasks, and trajectory export.

projects.name: Lume
projects.description: Creates and manages macOS and Linux virtual machines on Apple Silicon through Apple's Virtualization.Framework, providing local desktop environments for agents.

projects.name: E2B Desktop Sandbox
projects.description: Linux desktop templates and examples with screenshots, input, window control, and authenticated streaming; desktop SDK sources live in the E2B monorepo.

projects.name: E2B Open Computer Use
projects.description: Desktop agent application with a screen stream and interaction controls, executing tasks inside an E2B Linux sandbox; requires E2B service access.

projects.name: screenpipe
projects.description: Captures desktop activity into searchable local history and exposes context through APIs, MCP, and scheduled workflows; current source uses the Screenpipe Commercial License.

projects.name: Apache Maka (Incubating)
projects.description: Local-first agent workspace with an optional Computer Use runtime, snapshot-bound actions, native executor supervision, and durable execution records.

projects.name: Maka CU
projects.description: Native macOS execution layer used by Apache Maka's Computer Use runtime, with Maka-specific targeting and protocol integration.

projects.name: OpenClaw Built-in Computer Tool
projects.description: Capability-driven agent tool that observes through `screen.snapshot` and executes through `computer.act`. It binds coordinate actions to captured frames, returns post-action screenshots, and exposes only the action, target, observation, and delivery families advertised by the selected node provider.

projects.name: Peekaboo
projects.description: macOS CLI, menu-bar application, and MCP toolset with screen capture, accessibility inspection, native actions, and agent sessions; also integrates as an OpenClaw Computer Use provider.

projects.name: OpenClaw CUA Computer Provider
projects.description: CUA Driver-backed provider for desktop, window, and element control on macOS, Windows, and Linux. It also exposes browser preparation, navigation, element interaction, dialogs, downloads, file inputs, recording, and trajectory replay through execution-scoped opaque handles.

projects.name: OpenClaw Codex Computer Use Integration
projects.description: Prepares Codex app-server to discover, install, enable, and health-check the native Codex Computer Use MCP plugin. Codex owns the native tool calls; this path is separate from OpenClaw's Peekaboo and CUA node providers.

projects.name: OpenClaw Logbook
projects.description: Optional automatic work journal that samples screen snapshots, turns them into timestamped timeline cards, generates daily standup notes, and answers questions grounded in a tracked day's activity.

projects.name: Hermes Computer Use Toolset
projects.description: Model-agnostic `computer_use` tool for capture, app and window discovery, clicks, drag, scroll, typing, keys, value setting, and app focus. It supports screenshot, set-of-marks, and accessibility-tree observations, prefers background input, and returns structured verify-or-escalate verdicts after actions.

projects.name: Hermes CUA Driver Backend
projects.description: Cross-platform backend that runs CUA Driver as an MCP stdio service, maintains a session-scoped execution surface, and maps Hermes permission modes and approvals onto desktop actions. Installation, status, and structured diagnostics are available through `hermes computer-use`. The backend contains recording and trajectory-replay methods, but the public `computer_use` tool schema does not currently expose those actions.

projects.name: Hermes Browser Automation
projects.description: Separate browser toolset supporting Browser Use CLI, local Chromium over CDP, agent-browser, Lightpanda, Camofox, and Browser Use, Browserbase, or Firecrawl cloud sessions. It includes isolated sessions, optional real-profile snapshots, and local sidecars for private URLs.

projects.name: Pi Computer Use
projects.description: Pi Coding Agent extension that exposes desktop windows and managed CDP pages through one immutable, state-scoped interface. It combines macOS Accessibility, Windows UI Automation, and Linux AT-SPI2 semantics with platform-specific capture and policy-gated input for observation, search, checked actions, text reading, and UI-change waits.

projects.name: cc-haha
projects.description: Agent desktop workspace with local Computer Use, application permissions, macOS AX/CGEvent execution, and Windows screenshot/input execution; Linux packages do not imply Linux Computer Use support.

projects.name: Windows-MCP
projects.description: Windows MCP server exposing UIA observations, screenshots, input, window control, and system tools, with documented client integration, authentication, and tool restrictions.

projects.name: Playwright MCP
projects.description: Official Playwright MCP server for agents that operate Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit through structured accessibility snapshots and deterministic browser actions. It supports persistent browser context and rich page introspection without requiring a vision model.

projects.name: Playwright CLI
projects.description: Official token-efficient CLI and Agent Skill interface for Playwright. It provides snapshot refs, browser actions, named or persistent sessions, storage and network controls, screenshots, tracing, video recording, test generation, and a dashboard for monitoring or taking over agent sessions.

projects.name: OpenCLI
projects.description: Turns websites and Electron applications into deterministic commands while reusing the user's logged-in Chrome profiles. Its browser bridge exposes DOM snapshots, navigation, interaction, extraction, network inspection, tabs, screenshots, and adapter generation through CLI-oriented Agent Skills.

projects.name: CLI-Anything
projects.description: Framework and registry for generating agent-native CLI harnesses around desktop software, creative tools, engineering applications, and services. Generated harnesses use structured JSON, reusable Skills, tests, stateful sessions, and preview or trajectory loops so agents can operate application capabilities through deterministic commands.

projects.name: Better AX for Computer Use
projects.description: Developer Agent Skill for improving accessibility semantics in source-modifiable applications, with a partial Chromium AX audit tool and guidance for verifying focus, actions, and business effects.

projects.name: MacosUseSDK
projects.description: Native Swift library and CLI toolkit for traversing macOS Accessibility trees and operating other applications through AX actions or CoreGraphics input. It includes app discovery and activation, structured traversal, clicks, typing, keyboard input, scrolling, action-state diffs, and visual overlays for debugging. Tactile's macOS stack bundles and extends these lower-level primitives.

projects.name: Tactile
projects.description: Accessibility-first operating layer for agents that prioritizes AX or UIA semantics, falls back to OCR-grounded coordinates, and uses visual Computer Use when structured interfaces are insufficient. It includes a nine-tool macOS MCP facade plus macOS and Windows Skills for observation, input, bounded workflows, verification, app guides, traces, and evaluation.

projects.name: LongHorizon Harness
projects.description: Runs long-lived agents across desktop applications and terminals with recoverable state, progress verification, evaluation, and independent auditing.
